name: Tenant order export
scope: docs/designs/order-export.md at revision 3f9c2a1: tenant integrations request order exports and download them by signed link
summary: 15 threats on 7 flows, 5 of them cross a trust boundary: 10 mitigations (1 with evidence, 9 not run), 2 accepted risks and 3 backlog items. The design is a draft: no control is in place until built and tested. ASVS 4.0.3 level 2 review: 1 met, 11 gaps, 1 not applicable, 2 not examined.

flows.data: Export requests (POST /v1/exports: date range, format) and status requests (GET /v1/exports/{id}), each with an OAuth access token for a client credential

stride.information_disclosure: n/a: the requests hold a date range, a format and an export ID only; the signed link in the response is T4 on F6

flows.data: export.requested event: export ID, tenant ID, date range
Order rows for one tenant: customer name, delivery address, phone number, order lines

stride.repudiation: n/a: the read is a system action under the export ID that T3 audits
stride.elevation_of_privilege: n/a: the worker holds no user session; its read-only database role is part of T7

linddun.linking: n/a: rows go to the tenant that already holds them; no other data is joined
linddun.identifying: n/a: the tenant already knows these customers; identification is the purpose of the export
linddun.non_repudiation: n/a: order rows record purchases the tenant already holds
linddun.detecting: n/a: an internal read that no outside party can observe
linddun.non_compliance: n/a: retention of the result is T12 on F4

flows.data: Export CSV file with the order rows of one tenant

stride.repudiation: n/a: the file write is tied to its export ID; the request that caused it is audited in T3
stride.denial_of_service: n/a: files are deleted after 7 days (T12), which bounds storage growth; request volume is T5
stride.elevation_of_privilege: n/a: the worker identity can write only to export containers; part of T7

linddun.linking: n/a: the file holds one tenant's rows only and joins no other data
linddun.identifying: n/a: the file goes to the tenant that already knows these customers
linddun.non_repudiation: n/a: the file records orders, not actions a customer might wish to deny
linddun.detecting: n/a: file names are random export IDs that reveal nothing about customers

flows.data: Export file download through a signed link valid for 15 minutes

stride.repudiation: n/a: a download has no business effect; the request that made the file is audited in T3
stride.denial_of_service: n/a: a link serves one file from the managed storage endpoint; request volume is T5
stride.elevation_of_privilege: n/a: a signed link grants read on one file only (ADR-2)

linddun.linking: n/a: the download joins no other data
linddun.identifying: n/a: the file goes to the tenant that already knows these customers
linddun.non_repudiation: n/a: the download records no customer action
linddun.detecting: n/a: link and file names are random export IDs that reveal nothing about customers
linddun.non_compliance: n/a: retention is T12 on F4

flows.data: Responses: 202 with exportId to POST /v1/exports; export status and a signed link to the file, valid for 15 minutes, to GET /v1/exports/{id}

stride.spoofing: n/a: the client checks the API's public TLS certificate, the control of T2; the tenant is authenticated on the request, F1 (T1)
stride.repudiation: n/a: a response has no business effect of its own; the request that caused it is audited in T3
stride.elevation_of_privilege: n/a: a response grants no role; a link to another tenant's file is T6 under information disclosure

flows.data: export.requested v1 event: export ID, tenant ID, date range; the worker exports the tenant the event names

stride.repudiation: n/a: each event carries the export ID whose request T3 audits
stride.information_disclosure: n/a: the event holds IDs and a date range, no order data
stride.elevation_of_privilege: n/a: a forged or altered event is T14; the worker's rights on the database and storage are fixed by T7

threats.title: A stolen integration client secret is used to request exports
threats.mitigation: Existing (design, Context: OAuth client credential): OAuth client credentials. Planned: access tokens valid 15 minutes; client secrets kept in a key vault and rotated every 90 days
threats.verification: Integration test in CI: an expired or wrongly signed token gets 401; key vault rotation policy test

threats.title: A request or an export file is altered in transit
threats.mitigation: Existing (design, Context: HTTPS): HTTPS on the API. Planned: TLS 1.2 or later only on the API and the storage endpoint; HTTPS-only storage; HSTS on API responses
threats.verification: testssl.sh scan of both public endpoints in staging before each release: no protocol below TLS 1.2 and no plain HTTP

threats.title: A tenant denies having requested an export
threats.mitigation: Planned: one audit event per export request: client ID, tenant ID, export ID, UTC time and result
threats.verification: Integration test asserts one audit event for each POST /v1/exports

threats.title: A signed link pasted into a ticket or chat lets anyone download the file until it expires
threats.reason: ADR-2: links are bearer credentials by design, valid 15 minutes for one file; shorter links break slow tenant integrations
threats.accepted: Written acceptance in the design review record, 2026-11-18

threats.title: Mass export requests or status polling exhaust the API and the worker and load the orders database
Tenant A reads tenant B's export by its ID (insecure direct object reference)
threats.mitigation: Existing (design, Contracts GET /v1/exports/{id} and NFR-4): tenant taken from the access token, never the path; a foreign export ID or link returns 404. Planned: every lookup filters by tenant
threats.verification: NFR-4 automated test: tenant A requests tenant B's export ID and link, expects 404

threats.title: A leaked static secret lets an attacker act as the export worker against the database or storage
threats.mitigation: Existing (worker configuration at revision 3f9c2a1, checked by CI run 4182): workload identity for the worker; no password or account key in configuration. Planned: read-only database role on orders
threats.verification: CI policy test: the worker configuration holds no password or account key; secret scan on each pull request
threats.evidence: CI run 4182 on revision 3f9c2a1: policy test and secret scan passed, 2026-11-19

threats.title: The export query misses the tenant filter and mixes tenants' rows in one file
threats.mitigation: Planned: PostgreSQL row-level security by tenant; the worker sets the tenant from the event before it queries
threats.verification: Integration test with two seeded tenants: each export holds only its own rows

threats.title: Customer-entered text starting with =, +, - or @ runs as a formula when the tenant opens the CSV
threats.mitigation: Planned: prefix such cells with a single quote when the worker writes the file
threats.verification: Unit test with fixture rows that start with each of =, +, - and @

threats.title: An export container is readable without a signed link
threats.mitigation: Existing (design, Containers: one container per tenant): one container per tenant. Planned: containers private and public access disabled for the storage account
threats.verification: Infrastructure policy test in CI; an anonymous GET on a staging export file expects 403 or 404

threats.title: Exports carry phone numbers and full addresses that most tenants do not need
Export files with personal data are kept longer than needed
threats.mitigation: Existing (design, Containers and NFR-5: export files kept 7 days): deletion within 7 days. Planned: a storage lifecycle rule that deletes export files after 7 days
threats.verification: Lifecycle rule test in staging and a weekly scan for files older than 7 days

threats.title: End customers are not told that tenants export their order data
threats.reason: Tenants are the controllers; the data processing agreement makes them responsible for notice to their customers

threats.title: A process other than the Orders API puts or alters an export.requested event, so the worker exports any tenant's orders
threats.mitigation: Planned: queue access by workload identity only: the Orders API alone may send, the export worker alone may receive; no shared access keys on the queue
threats.verification: CI policy test on the queue's role assignments and key settings; a staging send with another workload identity expects 403

threats.title: Stored orders altered through the Orders API write paths, which this model does not examine, flow into export files

abuse_cases.actor: A former employee of a tenant who kept the integration client secret
abuse_cases.goal: Download all of that tenant's customer orders after leaving
abuse_cases.how: Requests a token with the old secret and calls POST /v1/exports

abuse_cases.actor: A user of tenant A who knows the export ID format
abuse_cases.how: Calls GET /v1/exports/{id} with guessed or leaked IDs

abuse_cases.actor: Anyone who sees a support ticket with a pasted download link
abuse_cases.goal: Download the export file before the link expires

review.reason: Integrations authenticate with client credentials, not user-set secrets; administrators sign in through tenant single sign-on, which is not examined here

review.evidence: CI run 4182 on revision 3f9c2a1: policy test shows the worker configuration holds no password or account key; secret scan passed, 2026-11-19

not_examined: Web UI and single sign-on for tenant administrators (needs its own model)
Orders API write paths and the integrity of stored orders
